item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Coupled with the frankly non-existent hook or intrigue to this article, in addition to the shallow premise and execution, this reads like a very poorly thought-out piece, and just leaves me feeling apathetic about it.

item.content:encoded: Dialogue is unbelievable. Perfect spelling, positively brimming with enthusiasm about being a foundation object. Take that character away and you just have a list of cutesy spells with an extremely lazy hook.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This seems so nonsensical for SCP-239 to have or need. I can't even picture a plausible scenario where this would be a thing. It's interesting only in theory, and fails horribly in execution and thought.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This is literally total lolFoundation. I don't see this document existing anywhere besides this wiki. If the killing spell were done away with, it'd be more believable as a means of keeping 239 in check until a permanent solution were reached, but as it is, it only limits her a little bit, and gives her the ability to kill people instantly. It's gotta be a downvote from me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It seems unrealistic for the Foundation to encourage a reality bender to practice magic. Even if the spell casting doesn't eventually go wrong and cause something bad, who's to say it won't realize that humans can't force a Type Green like it to do anything?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'd image that this girl grew up very, uniquely in the Foundation. I would to find more stories about her as an adult. (or at least older!) When does she, (if ever), figure out she's a reality bender and not a magic witch? Does it change much for her powers, or will she have already gotten her mind set on being limited to just the spells given to her?

As for this, I feel like it's old and not aged that well, but I'd hate for it to be deleted. For me, it's more the idea than the writing here that appeals.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Is this horrible? Yes. (I mean they give her a way to kill anyone, for heaven's sake). But I think it might be able to be fixed, primarily through less "hey look magic, let's be all fun and quirky and Harry potter ish" and more "hey, let's limit her powers to sheer uselessness and / or modify her behavior so that she can never be an actual threat".

You know, actually thinking about things, heaven forbid.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Seconding Roget and Thirding Orasmis, this doesn't feel like something the Foundation would do, and I can't think of a way it would be rewritten to better fit the modern tone of the Foundation.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This article has been placed up for review. Take the time to check it out, it turned out to be pretty cool.

This article seems like a relic from a past time. I basically concur with Orasmis, and add that this whole thing is bleauh. It was written by Dantenson because 239 was seen as being totally kawaii, which isn't really a viewpoint we take on humanoids these days. I just came away with a lot of bluh.

item.title: (no title)
